data.title: Thomson Reuters Named a Leader in IDC MarketScape for Compliant e-Invoicing
data.description:
Thomson Reuters is now the only provider named a Leader across four IDC MarketScape categories: value-added tax, sales and use tax, global trade, and e-invoicing.

TORONTO, Sept. 14, 2026 /CNW/ -- Thomson Reuters (TSX/Nasdaq: TRI), a global content and technology company, today announced that its e-invoicing and continuous transaction control (CTC) solution has been positioned as a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Compliant e-Invoicing 2026 Vendor Assessment (doc #EUR154882626, September 2026). Thomson Reuters was previously named a Leader in three IDC MarketScape reports for value-added tax*, sales & use tax*, and global trade**, which makes Thomson Reuters the only provider named a Leader across all four compliance categories.

"Being named a Leader again by IDC MarketScape is proof that our approach works: bringing tax determination, e-invoicing, continuous transaction controls, and regulatory intelligence together into one connected system is exactly the kind of innovation this market needs right now," said Ray Grove, Global Head of Product, at Thomson Reuters. "Compliance is becoming more digital, more continuous, and more fragmented every year, and we've built ONESOURCE Pagero to close those gaps before they become a challenge for our customers. That's what we believe leadership in this space looks like, and we intend to keep setting the pace."

Thomson Reuters ONESOURCE Pagero delivers e-invoicing and continuous transaction control (CTC) compliance across more than 90+ jurisdictions, serving more than 65,000 active e-invoicing customers today, connected through a business network that reaches approximately 14 million companies worldwide.

"Many organizations are moving beyond point compliance projects and looking for a more sustainable approach to managing e-invoicing obligations globally," said Kevin Permenter, Senior Director, Enterprise Applications Research at IDC. "Thomson Reuters brings together in-house regulatory expertise, global compliance coverage, and the scale and interoperability of the ONESOURCE Pagero network. That combination is particularly relevant for organizations looking to manage e-invoicing requirements consistently across diverse markets and trading ecosystems."

Notably, ONESOURCE Pagero was among the first few platforms accredited by the DGFiP as a Plateforme Agréée (the designation formerly known as PDP) and operates as the single Peppol access point for Chorus Pro, France's public B2G invoicing hub — meaning that as France's mandate comes into force, Thomson Reuters customers are ready to comply from day one.

ONESOURCE Pagero is part of Thomson Reuters portfolio of solutions meeting Fiduciary-Grade AI™ standards. It connects tax, trade, legal, and risk workflows on a single platform, combining e-invoicing and CTC with tax determination and regulatory intelligence. The result is a system that adapts as compliance requirements change, so customers are ready when new mandates take effect.

Thomson Reuters was also previously named a Leader in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Value-Added Tax Management Applications 2024 Vendor Assessment* (doc #US52732824, December 2024), the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide SaaS and Cloud-Enabled Sales and Use Tax Automation Software for Enterprise 2024 Vendor Assessment* (doc #US52035324, December 2024), and two 2025 IDC MarketScape reports for Worldwide Global Trade Management: IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Global Trade Management for Manufacturers and Exporters 2025 Vendor Assessment** (doc #US53604225, December 2025), and the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Global Trade Management for Retailers and Importers 2025 Vendor Assessment** (doc #US51573724, December 2025).

About IDC MarketScape

IDC MarketScape vendor assessment model is designed to provide an overview of the competitive fitness of technology and service suppliers in a given market. The research utilizes a rigorous scoring methodology based on both qualitative and quantitative criteria that results in a single graphical illustration of each supplier's position within a given market. IDC MarketScape provides a clear framework in which the product and service offerings, capabilities and strategies, and current and future market success factors of technology suppliers can be meaningfully compared. The framework also provides technology buyers with a 360-degree assessment of the strengths and weaknesses of current and prospective suppliers.

The company serves professionals across legal, tax, audit, accounting, compliance, government, and media. Its products combine highly specialized software and insights to empower professionals with the data, intelligence, and solutions needed to make informed decisions, and to help institutions in their pursuit of justice, truth, and transparency. data.title: PBF Energy Shares Fall on $500 Million Notes Offering
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

PBF Energy shares fell after the company said it plans to offer $500 million of exchangeable notes due 2032.

The stock slid 7% to $72.73 on Monday. Shares have still nearly tripled this year.

The petroleum refiner said it plans to offer the notes in a private offering exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933.

The notes will be co-issued by PBF Finance, a subsidiary of the company. The issuers expect to grant the initial purchasers an option to buy an additional $50 million aggregate principal amount of notes.

PBF plans to use the proceeds from the offering to fund the repayment of all of its 7.875% senior unsecured notes due 2030.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: WallachBeth Capital Announces Closing of Tenon Medical Warrant Inducement Offering for Aggregate Gross Proceeds of Approximately $2,872,338
data.description:
JERSEY CITY, N.J., Sept. 14, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- WallachBeth Capital LLC, a leading provider of capital markets and institutional execution services, announced today that Tenon Medical, Inc. () ("Tenon" or the "Company"), a medical device company dedicated to transforming care for patients with certain sacro-pelvic disorders has closed its previously announced warrant inducement agreement with an institutional investor to exercise outstanding warrants to purchase an aggregate of 572,179 of the Company's shares of common stock (the "Existing Warrants"). In consideration for the immediate exercise in full of the Existing Warrants for gross cash proceeds of $2,872,338.58, the exercising holder received new unregistered warrants (the "New Warrants") to purchase up to an aggregate of 858,269 shares of common stock (equal to 150% of the shares of common stock issued in connection with the exercise of the Existing Warrants) with an exercise price of $5.02 per share.  The New Warrants are immediately exercisable on the date of issuance and will expire five years from the date of issuance.

The gross proceeds from the warrant inducement were $2,872,338.58, excluding any proceeds that may be received upon the exercise of the New Warrants and before deducting financial advisor fees and other expenses payable by the Company.

WallachBeth Capital acted as financial advisor for the warrant inducement transaction.

The New Warrants described above were offered in a private placement pursuant to an applicable exemption from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Act") and, along with the shares of common stock issuable upon their exercise, have not been registered under the Act, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration with the Securities and Exchange Commission ("SEC") or an applicable exemption from such registration requirements. The Company has agreed to file a registration statement with the SEC covering the resale of the shares of common stock issuable upon exercise of the New Warrants (the "Resale Registration Statement").

This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy, nor will there be any sales of these securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of such jurisdiction.

The firm's experience includes initial public offerings, follow-on issues, PIPE offerings, and private transactions and ATM's.

data.title: TriMas Packaging to Showcase Global Beauty Packaging Capabilities at Leading Trade Shows This Fall
data.description:
TriMas Packaging, part of TriMas (NASDAQ: TRS), will showcase its global portfolio of dispensing, closure and customized packaging solutions for the fragrance, beauty and personal care markets at two of the industry's premier events this fall, LUXE PACK Monaco and Beautyworld Dubai.

LUXE PACK Monaco

  • Date: September 28-30, 2026
  • Location: Grimaldi Forum, Monaco
  • Booth: RD16, Ravel Hall

Beautyworld Dubai

  • Date: October 6-8, 2026
  • Location: Dubai World Trade Centre, Dubai, UAE
  • Booth: SR-G27

At both events, TriMas Packaging will feature a range of innovative packaging solutions designed to enhance functionality, aesthetics and the overall consumer experience. Featured products will include fragrance pumps, premium closures, dispensing systems and Singolo™, the Company’s fully recyclable all-plastic dispensing product line, demonstrating its commitment to innovation, customization and sustainability.

"These events provide excellent opportunities to connect with customers and showcase how TriMas Packaging's global capabilities help beauty and personal care brands turn innovative ideas into impactful packaging solutions," said Guilherme Lerro, Senior Vice President, Sales & Marketing. "With expertise spanning design, decoration and manufacturing, we partner with customers around the world to deliver packaging solutions that enhance brand identity, elevate consumer experience and support our customers' sustainability goals."

Visitors will also have the opportunity to experience product performance firsthand through interactive demonstration stations. These hands-on displays will highlight dispensing functionality, design flexibility and customization possibilities across TriMas Packaging's beauty and personal care portfolio.

About TriMas Packaging

TriMas Packaging designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of dispensing, closure and flexible packaging solutions serving leading brands across the beauty and personal care, fragrance and cosmetics, food and beverage, home care, pharmaceutical and nutraceutical, and industrial and agricultural markets. Powered by approximately 2,200 employees across 12 countries, TriMas Packaging partners with customers to deliver innovative, high-quality solutions that enhance how products are dispensed, protected, transported and stored, safely and securely, in an ever-changing marketplace. For more information, please visit www.trimaspackaging.com.

data.title: US senators weigh requiring AI giants to commit to preventing catastrophe
data.description:
By Courtney Rozen

U.S. Senate negotiators are debating legislation that would require AI companies to demonstrate they are taking reasonable precautions to keep their tools from causing harm, according to a Senate aide and a lobbyist familiar with the talks.

Alarm about the potential harm from AI grew last week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon said he had resigned, in part because the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade." AI-related stocks fell worldwide on Monday after leaders of some of the industry's largest companies called for slowing the pace of the technology's development.

The senators are debating giving the U.S. commerce secretary the power to request evidence that AI developers are taking reasonable steps to prevent harm, known as a “duty of care," according to the Senate aide and lobbyist. The secretary would also have the power to deploy government auditors to test companies' products themselves, they said. Reuters could not immediately determine what would qualify as “reasonable.”

The legislation is still being debated. Even if Congress approves the measure, it faces long odds of becoming law. U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday that existing authorities already provide adequate tools to regulate and prosecute tech companies, suggesting he wouldn't sign a bill setting new rules for AI.

The proposal is being discussed by Senate Majority Leader John Thune, Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz and Senator Amy Klobuchar, the top Democrat involved in the negotiations. Spokespeople for Thune and Cruz did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.

"I’m continuing to work toward a bipartisan agreement on legislation for government oversight of the greatest risks posed by AI models," Klobuchar said in a statement. "That includes requiring developers to work with government experts to verify and test models to make sure AI is safe."

data.title: Wizz Air CEO says it has no interest in airBaltic, other carriers at risk
data.description:
By Tim Hepher

Wizz Air sees few if any opportunities from airBaltic's bankruptcy and expects a wider shakeout of other European airlines that were unable to hedge against high fuel prices, the budget carrier's CEO Jozsef Varadi told Reuters on Monday.

The recent oil price spike "sucks up liquidity very quickly from the industry, and especially those airlines which are unhedged," Varadi said on the sidelines of a conference hosted by the International Society of Transport Aircraft Trading.

"I think they will be in a very difficult situation."

Planted at opposite ends of Europe's sprawling aviation market, Wizz and Latvian state-owned airBaltic have both been shaped by Europe's expansion eastwards over two decades followed by the collapse of relations with Russia.

"Now there are no Russians coming, and airBaltic is just far too big for a tiny little market like Latvia," Varadi said.

"Does it create an interest for us? Very limited to be honest ... Latvia is at the periphery of the European Union, then you have the Russian border. So given the current geopolitics how can you execute against that concept?"

Varadi co-founded Wizz in 2003 just as Hungary, Latvia and eight other countries were preparing to join the European Union. Moscow's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 dented its network but it has continued to grow at a significant pace.

AirBaltic, meanwhile, set out to become a regional hub airline but was left reeling by the loss of Russian routes and traffic as well as high fuel prices.

Airlines worldwide are grappling with high oil prices since the start of the Iran war. Wizz is hedged at half the market price across 80% of its needs in the next 12 months, Varadi told the ISTAT conference.

Varadi said this year would be bumpy as the industry tackles oil prices and geopolitics but could create opportunities.

"We've seen a vacuum in Italy. We were pushing a lot of capacity into Italy and in Romania, Albania and some other places, and I think we will continue to do that," he said.

data.title: Oracle, Corning, Alphabet, GE Vernova, CrowdStrike, SpaceX, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By George Glover and Mariapaula Gonzalez

Stocks dropped Monday after the bosses of Anthropic, OpenAI, and SpaceX called for a deceleration in AI development.

High-flying chip and memory stocks were getting hammered. Chip makers Intel and Advanced Micro Devices tumbled 6.3% and 6.1%, respectively. Coherent and Teradyne, a technology company that manufactures automated test equipment for microchips, were among the worst-performing stocks in the S&P 500.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise slumped 10% to $55.66. Beyond getting hit in the artificial-intelligence trade selloff, the stock was downgraded Monday by Evercore analysts to In Line from Outperform, who noted the outperformance this year hasn't left much room for upside. The firm, however, kept its price target unchanged at $65.

Tesla dropped 1.5%. CEO Elon Musk joined those concerned about humanity's ability to control AI and reposted a tweet on Saturday from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, saying he was "right."

Shares of software developers rallied-a slowdown in the AI buildout could reduce the threat of their industry being disrupted. Adobe, CrowdStrike, Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, and ServiceNow all jumped.

Oracle dropped 3.8% after co-founder Larry Ellison scrapped a plan to sell $7.5 billion worth of shares. Oracle has traded as a proxy for OpenAI's looming listing lately-but OpenAI CEO Sam Altman ruled out an initial public offering in 2026 in an interview published Saturday, citing AI safety fears.

Two Big Tech companies, however, could benefit from a slowdown in AI development. Alphabet-owned Google and Meta Platforms have been working on rival AI systems that compete with Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok. Alphabet rose 2.2% and Meta gained 2.1%.

SpaceX declined 1.6%. The stock was under pressure after AI leaders called for a development slowdown to reduce risks of an AI catastrophe. Though SpaceX's AI business is now expected to generate $60 billion in 2027 revenue-up from an estimate in July of $38 billion-exactly how AI revenue will play out is hard to say.

Corning tumbled 9.2% and was among the worst-performing stocks in the S&P 500. In the artificial-intelligence trade selloff, the stock was hit pretty hard. Corning and other optical networking companies have become a major part of the AI trade as the data-center buildout has increased demand for fiber-optic cables that transit data.

Iren fell 1.1%. J.P. Morgan analyst Richard Choe double upgraded the stock to Overweight from Underweight and raised his price target to $65 from $46. He cited momentum in the company's shift from Bitcoin to selling artificial-intelligence computing power.

Energy stocks jumped as the shutdown of a key pipeline in Saudi Arabia pushed up oil prices. Chevron added 1.1% and ExxonMobil climbed 1.2%. APA, ConocoPhillips, EOG Resources, and Occidental Petroleum also rose.

data.title: TransAlta Ordered by U.S. Government to Keep Washington Coal Unit Online for 90 More Days
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

TransAlta has received another order from the U.S. Department of Energy to keep Washington state's last coal-fired power plant operational for an additional 90 days.

The Calgary, Alberta-based power generator said Monday that its subsidiary TransAlta Centralia Generation received the order from federal regulators mandating that Unit 2 of its Centralia Generating Station remain available to support the grid.

The station is now ordered to remain available for operations until Dec. 12.

The power station was earmarked for closure at the end of 2025 as part of a shift toward cleaner sources to generate power but has received three other requests to keep the plant operational. The company had already retired Unit 1 at the end of 2020 as part of a state mandated two-phase closure of the coal-fired plant.

TransAlta said Monday that it will continue to comply with the directive while coordinating with state and federal officials.

data.title: Psychedelics Are Wall Street's Next Trip, and This Biotech Stock Is Already Up 200% — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Mackenzie Tatananni

First marijuana, then peptides-and now psychedelics are getting a second look, as Definium Therapeutics advances the case for medical LSD.

The drugmaker on Monday reported positive late-stage trial data for its fast-dissolving oral tablet, DT120, in patients with generalized anxiety disorder. The results marked the third positive Phase 3 readout for the drug this year and the second for anxiety specifically.

The trial met its main goal, showing significant improvement over placebo on the Hamilton Anxiety Rating Scale, a questionnaire gauging the severity of anxiety symptoms. It also met key secondary goals including improvement across two other clinician-rated scales.

Patients showed a 9.8-point improvement on the 56-point scale, called the HAM-A, 12 weeks after undergoing treatment. The placebo group, meanwhile, improved by just 4.7 points. Definium noted that the changes occurred rapidly, with improvement seen as early as the second day as treatment.

Shares rose 3.5% on Monday after spiking as much as 19% in premarket trading.

According to RBC Capital Markets analyst Brian Abrahams, the results appears to have exceeded Wall Street's expectations. The latest readout could reduce regulatory risk and unlock significant potential growth, "especially with the stock having pulled back into the results," he said.

Given the strength of the data to date across multiple well-designed studies, Abrahams believes Definium could file for approval for both generalized anxiety disorder and major depressive disorder.

Traditionally a party drug, LSD, or lysergic acid diethylamide, is currently classified as a Schedule I controlled substance, suggesting a high potential for abuse and no accepted medical use. Definium's DT120 contains a precise dose of lysergide D-tartrate, a salt form of LSD.

However, attitudes have been shifting towards drug's potential for decades, prompting a major re-evaluation in the medical community in the early 2000s.

Recent regulatory actions have also smoothed out the path ahead. President Donald Trump in April signed an executive order directing the Food and Drug Administration to accelerate access to treatments for patients with "serious mental illness," including complex and treatment-resistant conditions.

The directive placed psychedelic drugs directly in the regulatory line of sight. "The FDA subsequently announced a series of regulatory actions to support the development of what it called "perception-altering psychedelic medications," specifically serotonin-2A agonists, a class that includes LSD.

The directive aligns with a broader effort to overhaul drug regulations. Earlier this year, the Trump administration executed a radical shift in federal policy by reclassifying state-licensed marijuana as a less dangerous drug.

The administration has similarly championed popular therapeutic peptides, moving to ease restrictions and expand consumer access through compounding pharmacies despite safety warnings from scientists.

Altogether, these moves paint create a favorable backdrop for Definium. Jefferies analyst Andrew Tsai sees the narrative around DT120 "shifting to commercialization" following the latest readout, with potential approval by the end of next year.

Definium CEO Rob Barrow confirmed that the company was advancing toward a New Drug Application for DT120 and pointed to an upcoming meeting with regulators in the fourth quarter. Definium expects to file its application sometime in the first half of 2027.

data.title: BioNTech ADRs Gain on Positive Data From Lung Cancer Trial
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall

American depositary receipts of BioNTech were higher after the company said gotistobart, a lung cancer treatment, nearly doubled median survival in a Phase 3 trial.

BioNTech ADRs were up 3.7% to $110.34 as of midday Monday. They have risen 5.4% year-to-date.

The biotechnology company on Monday said gotistobart, developed in collaboration with OncoC4, demonstrated a median overall survival of 18.5 months in patients with squamous non-small lung cancer whose disease had progressed in prior treatments. That compares with a median overall survival of 10 months for standard-of-care chemotherapy, the company said.

"The magnitude of the survival benefit observed with gotistobart as a chemotherapy-free treatment approach in the PRESERVE-003 clinical trial is highly encouraging," said the study's principal investigator, Rama Balaraman. "If confirmed in the pivotal portion of the Phase 3 trial, these findings could transform the standard of care in a setting where new therapies are urgently needed."

The data came from the first stage of the Phase 3 trial. The second stage is ongoing at upwards of 160 sites globally, BioNTech said.

data.title: Global investment firm Carlyle extends reach in Canada; purchases oil and gas firm Parallax
data.description:
By Amanda Stephenson

Global investment firm Carlyle is expanding its reach in Canada through the acquisition of the privately owned Canadian oil and gas company Parallax.

  • The acquisition is the second in 12 months by Carlyle's energy group, which last year acquired Kiwetinohk Energy for approximately C$1.4 billion.

  • Carlyle has established a newly formed Canadian company called Avenrock Energy, which has reached a deal to acquire Parallax from Carnelian Energy Capital.

  • Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Sources pegged the total enterprise value of the deal at approximately C$1 billion and said Parallax's gross production is 20,000 boepd.

  • Parallax is an established Western Canadian company operating in the East Shale Duvernay in Alberta, with approximately 300,000 acres and a substantial production base focused predominantly on light oil and natural gas liquids.

  • Avenrock aims to establish a significant operating presence in Western Canada, with a focus on the continued development of the Parallax asset base to build out a leading Western Canadian light oil platform, according to a release.

data.title: Self-Improving AI Models Should Drive Compute Demand — Market Talk
data.description: Among the takeaways from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's calls this weekend to slow AI development was confirmation that Recursive Self Improvement, self-improving AI models, are being deployed across the industry, Melius Research analysts say in a research note. Amodei warned that the acceleration of RSI introduces a spate of new risks. But the admission is also a huge catalyst for compute demand, the analysts say. RSI runs on inference with thousands of agents constantly writing code, launching experiments and reading results, they say. Slowing upfront model training doesn't stop that loop, and arguably just redirects compute budgets elsewhere, the analysts say. "The models RSI produces are better and cheaper per token and every price cut in the last two months has been met with more consumption," they say. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

data.title: Charles Schwab to Bring Anthropic's Claude to Registered Investment Advisors

Charles Schwab is partnering with Anthropic to bring Claude to registered investment advisors.

The brokerage on Monday said its Schwab Advisor Services business will provide Anthropic's Claude for Financial Advisors offering to more than 16,000 independent RIAs.

Schwab said its unit is the first RIA custodian that is integrated with Claude for Financial Advisors, an Anthropic offering that assists advisors with tasks like financial plan updates, analytics, and client follow-up.

"Independent advisors have always succeeded on the strength of their relationships, and relationships are built on advice, service and client experiences that stand apart," Schwab Advisor Services head Jon Beatty said. "AI is exponentially powering the ability of advisors to stand apart in this way, even more so if it is integrated with the proprietary workflows and tech stacks advisors have already built."

data.title: PBF Energy Shares Fall on $500M Notes Offering
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

PBF Energy shares fell after the company said it plans to offer $500 million of exchangeable notes due 2032.

The stock slid 7% to $72.73 on Monday. Shares have still nearly tripled this year.

The petroleum refiner said it plans to offer the notes in a private offering exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933.

The notes will be co-issued by PBF Finance, a subsidiary of the company. The issuers expect to grant the initial purchasers an option to buy an additional $50 million aggregate principal amount of notes.

PBF plans to use the proceeds from the offering to fund the repayment of all of its 7.875% senior unsecured notes due 2030.
